Both traces solve the problem by following the same primary deduction chain: excluding all but Cy from S8, then applying a series of forward-chaining implications to assign S1, S7, S6, S3, S4, S5, and S2. Their approaches diverge in how they handle uncertainty and verify their work. Trace 1 performs one large hypothetical exploration (assuming S8 is Ed if certification rules are ignored) to justify the interpretation of the certification constraints, then later re-executes the entire implication chain to verify it. Trace 2, in contrast, performs a series of smaller, fragmented "What if" checks on individual steps (e.g., "What if S7 was not Ed?", "What if S4 was not Bo?") and re-checks the S8 candidacy multiple times. Both traces converge on the same final assignment, but Trace 1's divergence is a single comprehensive branch, while Trace 2's divergences are numerous local checks.

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's see if S8=Cy is forced even without the certification rules. Suppose S8 is not Cy." end="So S8 cannot be Ed. Same for S8 not being Ana, Bo, Di. So S8 must be Cy." basis=The solver opens a hypothetical branch where S8 is Ed (ignoring certification), explores the downstream assignments, and eliminates it because it violates Rule 3 and breaks the puzzle's uniqueness.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Is it possible that S1 is NOT Ana? If S8=Cy -> R7 is true." end="So Ana leads S1." basis=The solver briefly explores the alternative that S1 is not Ana and eliminates it by re-affirming the antecedent of Rule 7 is true.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Suppose I made a mistake in the implications." end="The logic holds up." basis=The solver re-executes the entire chain of implications from S8 to S2 verbatim, adding no new information or constraints beyond verifying the previous work.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Is it possible that S8 is led by someone who is 'not certified' but leads anyway?" end="So S8=Cy is the intended starting point." basis=The solver explores the branch where certification is just a fact and S8=Ed, finds it yields a valid but non-unique assignment, and explicitly eliminates this branch to maintain standard logic puzzle assumptions.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="What if S7 was not Ed? If S7 was not Ed, then Rule 4's antecedent is false" end="So S7 must be Ed. There is no alternative." basis=The solver explores the alternative that S7 is not Ed, traces it back to show it contradicts the established fact that S8 is Cy, and eliminates it.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="Is it possible that S1 is NOT Ana? If S8=Cy -> R7 is true." end="So Ana leads S1." basis=The solver explores the alternative that S1 is not Ana and eliminates it by re-affirming the implication of Rule 7.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="What if S4 was not Bo? If Bo does not lead S4, then Rule 2 doesn't trigger." end="So Bo leads S4 is a necessary consequence." basis=The solver explores the alternative that S4 is not Bo and eliminates it by re-affirming the implication of Rule 10.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Is it possible that S8 is not Cy? If S8 is not Cy, then rule 7's antecedent is false." end="So S8=Cy is a hard deduction." basis=The solver re-executes the S8 candidacy check already performed in the long CYCLE above, restating the same exclusions and conclusion without adding new constraints.
